This is SSI own managed multi-chain index issuance, not CEX holdings or a curator label. Only existing KYB-approved Whitelisted Participants can request mint/redeem for an assetID; catalog inclusion never enrolls a caller, grants issuer roles, obtains a maker quote or establishes legal/jurisdictional eligibility.

addMintRequest requires order.requester=msg.sender, membership, configured min/max index amounts and issue fee <= maxIssueFee, collected token fees, no rebalancing and a valid maker-signed order. It pulls each local-chain input ERC20 from the caller into the issuer, including the issue fee, records a PENDING request and locks index issuance. It does NOT mint immediately. Fixed swap validation/financial calls carry typed order data, not arbitrary target/selector/calldata execution.

addRedeemRequest requires the same eligibility and request gates plus current issuer role on the index token. It pulls caller-owned index shares into escrow; the input basket must exactly match the current index basket. Every output token must be local-chain and output destination must be this issuer. It records the pending request and locks issuance; no immediate burn or payout occurs.

Quote orderSign is a preexisting authorized MAKER signature, not a new wallet signing capability. Current Swap checks order hash, deadline, replay, maker role/signature, chain, allowlisted token identities and output addresses. Ordinary requests depend on mutable factory-selected token/swap contracts and owner/maker settlement. Underlying portfolio custody may span other chains; no bridge, other-chain target, maker execution, arbitrary trade/rebalance or authorization function is admitted.

Owner confirmMintRequest later finalizes swap transfers and mints only to the recorded requester. Owner confirmRedeemRequest later burns escrow and either pays net local-chain output directly to requester or credits claimables when force=true. Owner rejection can refund mint inputs directly or credit claims; redemption rejection returns escrow shares. These owner/maker functions are excluded. No settlement deadline, available liquidity, cancellation or guaranteed recovery is promised; source cancellation implementations are commented out and absent from ABI.

claim(token) pays only claimables[token][msg.sender], zeroes that credit and reduces aggregate reserved claims before sending the selected ERC20 to msg.sender. It cannot choose another owner or receiver, and is available only after owner-recorded claim credit. It is also whenNotPaused; a pending request is not itself a claimable amount.

Index amounts use 8 decimals. Input/output basket token quantities are floor(token.amount * order.inAmount/outAmount / 1e8) in each token base unit; issue fee floors token quantity * issueFee / 1e8, added at mint and subtracted at redeem. maxIssueFee caps the configured issue fee only, not custody spread, management fees, quote suitability or execution slippage. Order quantities/deadline are maker-quoted; there is no separate user min-output argument.

MAG7 issue fee reads zero and a nonempty preexisting participant list exists. Mutable point-in-time settings do not guarantee any caller eligibility or future enabled state.

Factory, swap and MAG7 are upgradeable dependencies; their current implementations and full matching implementation sources are retained. Factory owner may change issuers, swaps, fee managers, vault and token implementation subject to source gates. Selected ABI accepts assetID generally, but only the exact own SSI product resolved through current factory state is intended; no broad market coverage, backing or portfolio custody assurance is asserted. burnFor only destroys caller shares without proceeds and is excluded.

Markdown versions of documentation pages are available by appending `.md` to page URLs; this page is available as [Markdown](https://sosovalue-white-paper.gitbook.io/sosovalue-whitepaper/5.-sosovalue-indexes-new-approach-to-passive-crypto-investment-for-the-masses/5.3-solution-design.md). # 5.3 Solution Design ## Overview SSI(SoSoValue Indexes) Protocol leverages on-chain smart contracts to repackage multi-chain, multi-asset portfolios into Wrapped Tokens. These tokens represent a basket of underlying assets, enabling Wrapped Tokens to track the value fluctuations of the basket, achieving the effects of passive index investing. To achieve this, SSI Protocol integrates six types of participants to build a robust protocol ecosystem: 1. **User**: Investors who gain market beta/alpha returns by purchasing index tokens. 2. **UNI LP (Uniswap Liquidity Provider)**: Their primary role is to provide liquidity on Uniswap and earn transaction fees from Uniswap. 3. **WLP (Whitelist Participant)**: SSI index tokens through the protocol and balancing Uniswap market prices by buying/selling at market rates, aiming to align Uniswap prices with underlying asset value and earning arbitrage profits from price stabilization. 4. **PMM (Private Market Makers):** Helps purchase the underlying spot assets of index tokens and stores them in custody accounts. 5. **Custody**: Ensures the secure storage of the underlying assets of index tokens. 6. **Index Compiler:** Responsible for formulating the index construction methodology, determining the constituent tokens and weights, and ensuring the long-term effective operation of the index. ## **Index Token Minting** Before minting, WLP needs to send a quote request to Protocol Server, which will return a quote order. 1. If the order price is favorable, WLP can apply minting with the order on-chain. Cash will be transferred to the Protocol Contract first. 2. The Protocol will verify the order and inform PMM to fill the order. 3. Once PMM receives the order request, PMM will send the underlying tokens to our Custodian Wallets. 4. After verifying the transfers, the Protocol will transfer cash to PMM and mint SSI token to WLP. ## **Index Token Burning** Before Burn, WLP needs to send a quote request to Protocol Server, which will return an order. 1. If the order price is favorable, WLP can apply Burn with the order on-chain. SSI token will be transferred to the Protocol Contract first. 2. The Protocol will verify the order and inform PMM to fill the order. 3. Once PMM receives the order request, PMM will transfer cash to the Protocol Contract. 4. Then Protocol will withdraw the underlying tokens from Custodian Wallet to PMM. 5. After verifying the transfers, Protocol will burn SSI tokens and transfer cash to WLP. ## **Rebalance** The protocol enters the rebalancing state and pauses minting and burning operations. 1. The protocol first fetches the target index constituent token information, including rebalancing details, from the index compiler. 2. The protocol server sends a rebalancing quote request to PMM, which will return a quote order. 3. If the order price is favorable, the protocol will verify the order and notify PMM to fill the order. 4. During the rebalancing process, tokens are transferred between the protocol's custody wallet and PMM wallets. PMM will sell the tokens being removed from the index and buy the tokens being added. This process is secured by on-chain smart contracts to ensure the trustworthiness of the transactions. 5. After all trades are completed, the protocol updates the index token constituent information and marks the rebalancing process as complete. 6. Once the rebalancing process is complete, minting and burning operations resume. ## **WLP** In the SoSoValue Indexes Protocol, Whitelisted Participants (WLPs) play a crucial role in maintaining the secondary market price of SSI tokens in alignment with the underlying asset value. Each WLP undergoes a KYB verification process, and upon approval, gains the right to mint and redeem SSI tokens. When price discrepancies arise in the secondary market, WLPs can arbitrage the spread between the market price and the mint/redeem price, helping to bring the secondary market price back in line with the intrinsic value of the underlying assets. For example, if buying pressure drives the secondary market price of MAG7.ssi up to $1.02 while its underlying asset value remains at $1.00, a positive premium of approximately 2% emerges. In this scenario, WLPs can mint new MAG7.ssi tokens at close to $1.00 using USDC and sell them in the secondary market at $1.02, capturing a 2% arbitrage profit. While generating arbitrage gains, WLPs also contribute to expanding the total circulating supply of MAG7.ssi and increasing the protocol’s Asset Under-Management (AUM). ## **Key Addresses (Base Chain)** **Indexes Token Addresses**\ MAG7.ssi: 0x9E6A46f294bB67c20F1D1E7AfB0bBEf614403B55\ DEFI.ssi: 0x164ffdaE2fe3891714bc2968f1875ca4fA1079D0\ MEME.ssi: 0xdd3acDBDc7b358Df453a6CB6bCA56C92aA5743aA\ USSI: 0x3a46ed8FCeb6eF1ADA2E4600A522AE7e24D2Ed18 **Contract Addresses**\ swap: 0xF909bfa750721501B4F8433588FaE5cE303Db08B\ factory: 0xb04eB6b64137d1673D46731C8f84718092c50B0D\ issuer: 0x0306acEb4c20FF33480d90038F8b375cC6A6b66e\ rebalancer: 0x84663e30973D552ac357FD04F3Ac6ebbD495Ab15\ feeManager: 0x2E469365030F068eCB1176a0D5600bA470Cf07A9\ stakeFactory: 0x585834242BB31427B1dC7486DD4BDe7c724e35c1\ assetLocking: 0x935A4B1F6F3E891a226b2522ac22d45Ce5839383\ Protocol OWNER: 0xd463D3d8333b7AD6a14d00e1700C80AF5A37F751 (cobo custody)
